headline: Iceland restart lifts volumes and earnings sharply
summary_short: Net sales were $961.2M, up 27.8% q/q on higher shipments after the Grundartangi Line 2 restart. Net income was $302.6M ($2.89 diluted) and adjusted EBITDA was $331.6M.
summary_long: Higher shipments from the Grundartangi Line 2 restart and favorable realized metal prices drove sales. Net income benefited from $31.0M of net exceptional items, mainly unrealized derivative gains and an insurance gain, partly offset by Iceland equipment-failure costs. Adjusted EBITDA rose $4.7M q/q, with volume and price gains offset by higher operating costs and unfavorable power price realization in extreme heat. Liquidity was $1,161.5M including $713.0M of cash. The company expects Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $275M to $300M.
confidence_notes: Adjusted net income, adjusted EPS and adjusted EBITDA are non-GAAP. Net income includes net exceptional items and an insurance gain. y/y net sales delta uses the prior-year value from the shard (Yahoo timeseries); q/q figures come from the release.

drivers.explanation: Higher shipments from Line 2 at Grundartangi returning to near full production, plus favorable realized metal prices.
Line 2 at Grundartangi returned to near full production during the quarter after its restart.
Higher shipments and prices, partly offset by a smaller insurance gain and unfavorable power price realization from extreme hot weather.
Favorable sales volume and mix and realized metal prices, offset by higher operating expenses and unfavorable power price realization.
